draft.title: Viking raids
card: In 793, Vikings attacked the monastery at Lindisfarne, an island off the coast of northeast England. This raid is often taken as the start of the Viking Age.
Monasteries held silver, gold and other treasures. They were usually undefended, because the monks were not fighters.
Longships let raiders land without warning, take what they could carry and leave before local forces arrived.
Raids went on for centuries. They struck many places across the British Isles and Europe, wherever wealth was easy to take.
draft.remember: Vikings raided places that were rich and poorly defended, and Lindisfarne in 793 is where the attacks are said to have begun.

a.q: Why was a monastery such as Lindisfarne a good target for Viking raiders?
opts: It held treasure but had little protection
It held an army but had little treasure
It was close to Scandinavia but had no coast
It was a rival kingdom but had weak leaders
a.why: Monasteries held treasure and had few people able to fight, so raiders could take wealth with little risk. Lindisfarne was not an army base or a kingdom, so the other options do not fit what the card says.
a.clue: Think about what a monastery held and who guarded it.

b.q: A Viking crew spots a coastal village in Europe. It has a store of silver and no soldiers. What would the crew most likely do?
opts: Land quickly, take the silver and sail away
Wait for a large army to arrive before landing
Sail past because only armies held wealth
Settle there at once and farm the land
b.why: Raiders chose rich places with poor defences, and their longships let them strike fast and leave. Settling is a different Viking activity, and it does not match a quick raid on a village with silver.
b.clue: Rich and poorly defended places were the usual targets.

a.best: It held treasure but had little protection

b.best: Land quickly, take the silver and sail away

check.summary: No problems found. The facts on Lindisfarne in 793 and on why monasteries were targets are accurate, and each question has exactly one defensible answer.
